domain_setting: A friendly neighborhood retail district and checkout setting. Use storefronts, market stalls, service counters, online ordering, price comparison, payment and clothing fitting as appropriate.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use 304×192 scenes with one clear shopping action, service or retail venue as the central cue; avoid readable text and numerals.
Distinguish store types by their signature goods: bread, books, fashion, meat, prepared foods, cleaning, fish, flowers, produce, tools, jewelry, shoes and toys.
Keep butcher and fish seller scenes calm and non-graphic; a seller, display counter and merchandise teach the shop role.
Flea market is a casual secondhand market with mixed wares; street market is a row of outdoor vendor stalls with produce or goods.
Store is a larger general retailer with broad merchandise and cart; shop is a smaller focused storefront; mall is a multi-store indoor complex.
Separate action direction: buy/pay to seller, sell from vendor, return/refund back to shop, exchange one item for another, pickup versus delivery.

Differentiate price concepts: bargain hunting/shop around compare offers; haggle is a buyer and seller negotiating; discount, fifty percent off, sale and slash prices show price reductions; rip-off is unfair overcharging.
For checkout, distinguish bank as financial institution, bank card/card as payment card, cash as notes and coins, receipt as proof of purchase, checkout as payment lane, refund as money returned.
Clothing group should show color swatches, fitting-room curtain, garment size measurement, try-on and whether a garment fits properly.
Use calm, ethical retail scenes; no readable signage, prices, branded logos or distressed customers.

polysemy_resolution_table.baker: A person who bakes or sells bread and pastries; show the baker with finished goods, not just a loaf.
polysemy_resolution_table.butcher: A meat seller working at a counter; keep the scene non-graphic and avoid slaughter.
polysemy_resolution_table.fish dealer: A fish supplier/vendor in a market context, distinct from a fishmonger serving customers at a retail counter.
polysemy_resolution_table.fishmonger: A seller at a fish shop counter with fresh whole fish on ice; not a fisherman or a cooked seafood plate.
polysemy_resolution_table.flea market: An outdoor or indoor market for secondhand goods and mixed small wares; not an insect infestation.
polysemy_resolution_table.florist: A flower seller arranging bouquets; distinguish from a greengrocer selling produce.
polysemy_resolution_table.greengrocer: A retailer selling fresh fruits and vegetables; show produce and a market stall/shop.
polysemy_resolution_table.hardware store: A shop selling tools and household hardware; not an electronics shop or factory.
polysemy_resolution_table.jewelers: A jewelry shop with a display case and fine items; avoid a lone person wearing jewelry.
polysemy_resolution_table.mall: A shopping center with multiple stores and shared walkways, following the shop-seller group context even though the source Japanese gloss points to a shaded promenade.
polysemy_resolution_table.store: A large general retailer with broad aisles or a shopping cart; distinguish from the small focused shop.
polysemy_resolution_table.street market: Outdoor rows of seller stalls and shoppers; distinguish from the secondhand flea market.
polysemy_resolution_table.bargain-hunting: A shopper comparing offers to find a good price; not haggling with a seller.
polysemy_resolution_table.buy: A customer gives payment and receives an item.
polysemy_resolution_table.sell: A seller hands merchandise to a buyer and receives payment; opposite direction from buy.
polysemy_resolution_table.choose: Selecting one item from several similar options.
polysemy_resolution_table.delivery: Goods sent to the customer by courier; distinct from a customer collecting an order.
polysemy_resolution_table.exchange: Replace one purchased item with another; not a currency exchange.
polysemy_resolution_table.fit: A garment is the correct size and shape for a person; show the clothing fit, not a furniture installation.
polysemy_resolution_table.haggle: A buyer and seller negotiate the price; not simply browse or compare prices.
polysemy_resolution_table.online shopping: A person orders items on a digital screen for delivery or pickup.
polysemy_resolution_table.pickup: Collect a prepared order at a counter or locker; distinguish from delivery.
polysemy_resolution_table.shop around: Compare several shops or offers before deciding; related to but distinct from bargaining over one price.
polysemy_resolution_table.try on: A person tests clothing in a fitting room; distinguish from whether it fits properly.
polysemy_resolution_table.want: Desire for an item, shown by attention/choice; avoid readable thought bubbles or text.
polysemy_resolution_table.return: Take an item back to the shop after purchase; distinct from a refund of money.
polysemy_resolution_table.fifty percent off: Exactly half-price concept shown with a half/paired price tag visual, with no numerals or text.
polysemy_resolution_table.good deal: A purchase that offers strong value; distinguish from an explicit percentage reduction.
polysemy_resolution_table.on a tight budget: Carefully choosing affordable necessities with a limited set of coins; no hardship stereotype.
polysemy_resolution_table.overpriced: An item priced higher than comparable alternatives; show price comparison without text or numbers.
polysemy_resolution_table.percentages: A percentage idea as a mathematical price fraction; use a pie/fraction visual, not digits.
polysemy_resolution_table.rip-off: Unfair overcharging for an item; show a suspiciously mismatched price comparison without depicting criminal threat.
polysemy_resolution_table.slash prices: A retailer reducing prices across merchandise; use crossed-down tags without numerals or readable text.
polysemy_resolution_table.discount: A reduced price on a single item; distinguish from a broad sale and the exact half-off term.
polysemy_resolution_table.price: Money amount requested for an item; no readable numerals or text.
polysemy_resolution_table.sale: A retail event with multiple reduced items; distinct from the action of selling.
polysemy_resolution_table.bank: A financial institution in the paying group, not a river bank.
polysemy_resolution_table.card: A bank/payment card used at checkout, not a playing or greeting card.
polysemy_resolution_table.cash: Paper notes and coins used directly for payment.
polysemy_resolution_table.checkout: A shop payment lane with register and goods; not merely a counter.
polysemy_resolution_table.pay: Hand money or tap a card to settle a purchase.
polysemy_resolution_table.receipt: A printed proof of a completed purchase; not an invoice or price list.
polysemy_resolution_table.refund: Money returned to a customer after a return; distinct from returning the item.
polysemy_resolution_table.color: Clothing color choices shown by garments or swatches; no written color names.
polysemy_resolution_table.fitting room: A private changing booth in a clothing shop, with curtain and mirror.
polysemy_resolution_table.size: The measurement/scale of clothing, shown with size comparisons or a measuring tape; distinguish from color.

glossary_context_notes: Live course groups establish shopping-context senses for bank (Paying and checkout) and mall (Types of shops and sellers), despite source Japanese glosses that suggest river bank and a shaded promenade.
Exact-key and near-synonym candidate renders were reviewed at work/vocab-art/review/lesson-73-candidates.png; asset decisions are documented in existing_asset_triage.

Batch 1 retained the clear bookshop storefront and butcher counter; the baker is shown working beside oven and bread, boutique has a fashion mannequin/handbag, and delicatessen has a staffed prepared-food display. Replaced a misleading cross-shaped boutique mark after review.

Batch 2 distinguishes dry cleaning/pressing from home laundry, fish dealer at a market crate stall from fishmonger serving a retail customer, secondhand flea-market wares from fresh-goods street market, and florist flowers from greengrocer produce. Replaced a cross-shaped flea-market object with a vintage clock after review.

Batch 3 used the previously reviewed indoor shopping-mall atrium for mall; authored a produce seller with scales, hardware tools, jewelry display and shoe shop. Redesigned the shoes after review for clear side-profile silhouettes. Rejected the grocery-store aisle as a greengrocer match because it did not show a seller.

Batch 4 reused the reviewed large general-store cart scene. Street market is fresh stalls while flea market is secondhand wares; toy store has toys; bargain hunting compares matching goods and coin-count price tags; buy shows goods moving to the customer during payment.

Batch 5 reused the reviewed suit-fit illustration. Choose shows selection from several products; delivery shows a parcel being handed to a recipient at the door; exchange swaps one garment for another; haggle now shows buyer and seller making different coin offers with a back-and-forth arrow.

Batch 6 reused the reviewed shopping-street activity scene. Online shopping is shown on a laptop; pickup is collection of a prepared bag at the shop counter; sell focuses on the shopkeeper receiving coins as goods go to a customer; shop around compares the same bag at two stores with different coin-count prices.

Batch 7 follows the shopping sense of return as taking an item back to the shop, distinct from a refund. Try on shows clothing being checked in a fitting-room mirror; want focuses attention on one desired shop item. Fifty percent off compares four coin marks to two and includes a split-coin cue; good deal pairs a quality item and modest coin price with approval marks, without implying a percentage.

Batch 8 shows budget-conscious essential shopping with three coins and a small wallet, bread and an apple; overpriced uses matching goods with two versus six coins; percentages use a 100-cell grid and a fractional circle; rip-off shows a tiny item weighed against many coins with a wary shopper; slash prices shows a retailer striking through multiple tags.

Batch 9 keeps bank as the financial institution (the payment group overrides its conflicting riverbank Japanese gloss); the direct bank art has the secure vault/teller cues. Discount is a coupon-style reduction for one item; price is a plain attached tag; sale is a retail event with multiple reduced goods; card is a payment card at a checkout terminal.

Batch 10 reused the reviewed physical-cash, general pay and completed-sale receipt scenes. Checkout is a self-service payment lane with conveyor, scanner and terminal; refund shows the item going to the clerk while coins flow back to the customer, distinct from the item-return action alone.

Batch 11 added the same three shirt styles in different colors and a curtained fitting-room booth. Reused the measuring-tape size comparison after recoloring all three garments uniformly blue so the scale cue does not compete with color.
